humidityNotes: Prefers average to high humidity; mist occasionally or use a pebble tray.
careTips: Thrives in bright, indirect light. Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil are dry. Wipe leaves to keep them dust-free. Rotate periodically for even growth.

humidityNotes: Tolerates dry air well; no extra humidity needed.
careTips: Extremely forgiving. Tolerates low light and neglect. Let the soil dry fully between waterings; root rot is the main risk. Feed once in spring.
diagnosisChecklist: [{"symptom": "Mushy, translucent base", "causes": ["Overwatering / root rot — stop watering, repot in dry mix"]}, {"symptom": "Wrinkling leaves", "causes": ["Severely underwatered", "Root bound"]}, {"symptom": "Leaves falling over", "causes": ["Too little light", "Overwatering"]}]

humidityNotes: Average household humidity is fine.
careTips: Grows in almost any light condition. Water when the top soil is dry. Trims easily and roots in water for propagation.

humidityNotes: Enjoy extra humidity; group with other plants or run a humidifier nearby.
careTips: Loves bright, filtered light and stable conditions. Keep away from drafts and radiators. Water when the top 2 cm of soil are dry; feed monthly in growing season.
diagnosisChecklist: [{"symptom": "Dropping leaves after a move", "causes": ["Stress from changed light or drafts — usually recovers"]}, {"symptom": "Brown spots with yellow halo", "causes": ["Overwatering", "Poor drainage"]}, {"symptom": "Brown, dry leaf edges", "causes": ["Low humidity", "Underwatering"]}]

humidityNotes: Appreciates some humidity; brown tips often mean the air is too dry.
careTips: Easy-going and pet-safe. Bright, indirect light suits it best. Water when the top soil dries; flush the pot occasionally to clear fertilizer salts.

humidityNotes: Happy in dry air; stores water in its rhizomes.
careTips: Near-unkillable. Tolerates low light and long dry spells. Water sparingly - let the soil dry out fully between drinks.

humidityNotes: Loves humidity; mist regularly in winter.
careTips: Droopy leaves are a clear signal it is thirsty. Prefers shade to bright sun. Keep the soil lightly moist but never waterlogged.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry air; avoid misting.
careTips: A sunny windowsill is ideal. Water deeply but infrequently - let the soil dry completely between waterings. Use a gritty, fast-draining mix.

humidityNotes: Demanding: needs high humidity or leaf edges brown fast.
careTips: Keep evenly moist, never waterlogged. High humidity and filtered or rainwater only — leaf tips brown with tap water. Keep away from direct sun.
diagnosisChecklist: [{"symptom": "Crispy brown leaf margins", "causes": ["Low humidity", "Minerals or chlorine in tap water"]}, {"symptom": "Leaves curling inward", "causes": ["Underwatering", "Heat stress"]}, {"symptom": "Faded leaf patterns", "causes": ["Light too strong"]}]

humidityNotes: Fine in dry indoor air.
careTips: A succulent: water deeply but rarely and let soil dry fully. Bright light keeps it compact. Repot every 2-3 years; toxic to pets.
diagnosisChecklist: [{"symptom": "Shrivelled, soft leaves", "causes": ["Underwatering", "Root damage"]}, {"symptom": "Black, mushy stems", "causes": ["Root rot from excess water"]}, {"symptom": "Lost bottom leaves only", "causes": ["Normal aging of an established plant"]}]

humidityNotes: Appreciates occasional misting in dry rooms.
careTips: Wants the brightest window you have. Split mature rootballs to propagate. Leaves split naturally in low humidity — cosmetic only.

humidityNotes: Likes steady household humidity; avoid cold drafts.
careTips: Water from the bottom or around the crown — water on leaves spots them. Warm water only. Bright indirect light keeps blooms coming.

humidityNotes: Average room humidity is fine.
careTips: Not a desert cactus: keep slightly moist in growth. Cool, dark nights in autumn trigger blooms. Cuttings root easily in water.

humidityNotes: High humidity; crisps up fast in dry air.
careTips: Bright indirect light and well-draining chunky mix. Sensitive to cold: keep above 15 C. Dormant in winter — cut watering back hard. Toxic to pets and children.

humidityNotes: Average household humidity is fine; appreciates occasional misting.
careTips: Bright indirect light and rotate for even growth. Water when the top layer of soil is dry and wipe dusty leaves. Sensitive to cold drafts.

humidityNotes: High humidity strongly preferred; dry air turns fronds brown.
careTips: Keep the soil evenly moist, never soggy. A bright bathroom or pebble tray works wonders. Trim brown fronds at the base.

humidityNotes: Average humidity; brown tips usually mean dry air or tap-water salts.
careTips: Water when the top few cm of soil are dry. Sensitive to fluoride in tap water - filtered water prevents tip burn. Tip cuttings root easily.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry air; average room conditions are ideal.
careTips: Water sparingly - the plump pearls store water. Give bright light and a very gritty mix. Press stem cuttings onto the soil to propagate.

humidityNotes: No humidity needs; likes dry air.
careTips: Lots of direct sun, infrequent watering and fast-draining soil keep the rosettes compact. Water at the base, not into the crown.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry air; normal room conditions suit it.
careTips: Soak thoroughly, then let the soil dry completely. Tolerates lower light than most succulents. Offsets can be potted up year round.

humidityNotes: Appreciates humidity; mist in winter near radiators.
careTips: One of the best low-light palms. Keep slightly moist and feed monthly during growth. Brown frond tips mean thirst or dry air.

humidityNotes: Average room humidity is fine.
careTips: Water when the top 5 cm of soil is dry. Bright indirect light keeps the leaves glossy. Tolerates hard pruning to shape the braided trunk.

humidityNotes: Average to high; tolerant of room air.
careTips: Fast, forgiving trailing plant. Water when the topsoil dries. Variegation fades in low light - move brighter to keep the stripes strong.

humidityNotes: Loves higher humidity; a pebble tray keeps the big leaves firm.
careTips: Keep evenly moist in bright light - pink colour deepens with more light. Cut back long vines to encourage bushiness.

humidityNotes: Happy in average room air.
careTips: Treat like a succulent: dry out between waterings and give bright light for blooms. Never cut off spent flower spurs - the next blooms reuse them.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry to average air.
careTips: Water when the little hearts start to wrinkle. The potato-like tubers hate wet feet, so use a chunky, fast-draining mix.

humidityNotes: Average room humidity is fine.
careTips: Glossy, compact and easy. Let the topsoil dry between waterings. Dropping or yellow leaves mean overwatering, not thirst.

humidityNotes: Loves humidity; dry air invites spider mites.
careTips: Keep evenly moist in bright, filtered light. Flush the soil once a year to wash out fertilizer salts.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry air.
careTips: Very drought tolerant: full sun to bright light, water deeply, then let the soil dry out completely. Rotate so it grows straight.

humidityNotes: Needs steady humidity; mist or use a pebble tray.
careTips: Colour lives on light: several hours of direct sun keeps the leaves red and orange. Keep evenly moist and avoid moving it - it sulks.

humidityNotes: Average to high; misting keeps the leaves rich green.
careTips: Fast and bold. Water when the topsoil dries. The sap irritates skin and mouths, so keep well away from pets and children.

humidityNotes: Average room humidity is fine.
careTips: Turn the pot weekly for a symmetrical shape and water when the topsoil is dry. The baby plantlets can be rooted in water or potted straight up.

humidityNotes: Prefers dry air.
careTips: Water only when the stems begin to shrivel. The fleshy segments detach at a touch, so repot rarely - and into a deep pot for long tails.

humidityNotes: Likes some humidity; great for a cool bedroom.
careTips: Prefers a cool room and bright light. Let the top inch dry between waterings. Check for spider mites in warm, dry air.

humidityNotes: Average room humidity is fine.
careTips: Trailing, fast and colourful. Pinch back to keep it bushy and water when the topsoil dries. The purple-silver colours bleach out in dim spots.

humidityNotes: Needs steady humidity; dry air crisps the leaf edges.
careTips: Folds its leaves up at night. Keep lightly moist and warm; curling leaves signal thirst or cold drafts.

humidityNotes: Loves high humidity.
careTips: Thirsty and hungry in growth season: keep moist, feed often. In winter the tuber can rest cooler and almost dry, then wakes with water.

humidityNotes: Loves humidity, but avoid wetting the fuzzy leaves.
careTips: Grow it for the leaves and remove the plain flowers. Keep barely moist - the hairy rhizomes rot easily in wet soil.

humidityNotes: Loves humidity; grouping plants helps.
careTips: Soak the bark weekly and drain fully - never let it sit in water. A slight autumn drop in night temperature triggers new flower spikes.

humidityNotes: Prefers high humidity; brown needles mean dry air.
careTips: A bright, cool room is best. Keep slightly moist - it hates drying out - and avoid chlorine-based fertilizers.

humidityNotes: Average humidity is fine; occasional misting helps.
careTips: Let the topsoil dry between waterings. Yellowing, dropping leaves are almost always overwatering. Prune hard to keep it bushy.

humidityNotes: Handles dry air as well as humid corners.
careTips: Nearly unkillable: low light, low water, total neglect. Wipe the leaves occasionally and it forgives almost everything else.

humidityNotes: Loves humidity; dry air yellows the feathery fronds.
careTips: Soft, feathery and a bit thirsty - keep lightly moist. The red berries are toxic if eaten. Cut old stems to the base in spring.

humidityNotes: Appreciates humidity; mist in winter.
careTips: Vivid strap leaves need bright light. Water when the top layer dries, and use filtered water to prevent brown tips.
